newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Novorossiisk oil port repair date not yet set.
newsitem.headline: Novorossiisk oil port repair date not yet set.

text.p: The largest crude oil loading berth in Russia's main export terminal of Novorossiisk may close for maintenance for up to 16 days in December, but oil export levels will not be affected, port sources said on Tuesday.
Two port officials said no decision had yet been taken on precisely when and for how long to close berth number one, which is the largest of the port's crude oil loading berths.
"We have other berths, so total export levels will not be affected," said Oleg Lesnetsky of the port's engineering section.
Gennady Serota of the oil berths department said the trunk pipeline feeding the berth would undergo maintenance at the same time, adding that total repairs could last 16 days.
"This maintenance will undoubtedly take place, but it will in no way affect the port's capacity," he said.
Both men said they did not know when officials would decide on dates for the repairs.

London-based traders have said berth number one's closure could cause the price of Russian Urals crude oil to rise, since exporting smaller cargoes of oil from Novorossiisk's other, smaller berths carries higher freight costs.
Novorossiisk's crude oil storage tank capacity, crucial when pipeline repairs are carried out, is estimated at between 500,000 tonnes (3.65 million barrels) and 700,000 tonnes (5.10 million barrels).
